{"description":"When a Decision reaches `accepted` from anything else, or a GOVERNED_BY edge is drawn to an already-accepted Decision, the reply carries a `settled_question_prose` block: each governed node whose prose still asserts the question is open, the phrase that matched, and an excerpt QUOTED AROUND THE MATCH so the reader sees the words that fired rather than the node's opening paragraph.

THE SIBLING OF `cap:a-status-advance-says-whether-its-prose-predates-it`, and built on its reasoning rather than beside it. That one catches a STATUS outrunning its own description inside one node. This one catches PROSE OUTRUNNING A DECISION THAT GOVERNS IT across an edge — the same rot, one relation out.

BOTH TRIGGER MOMENTS ARE COVERED, and that is a design choice with a reason: the decision may be settled first and the edge drawn afterwards, which is the ordering the incident that prompted this actually had available. A hook on the status setter alone would have missed it entirely.

WHY A REPLY AND NOT A DETECTOR, measured before building rather than argued: over reflow2's own design, 48 of 640 governed nodes carry one of these markers somewhere in their prose, and a good share are legitimate — a node that QUOTES an old question, or discusses a different one in a long statement. As a sweep that is 48 findings of mixed quality, which is the noise that gets switched off in a week. Fired when somebody accepts the decision or draws the edge, it is one node in front of the person who just moved it.

⚠️ HONEST LIMITS, both real and neither hidden. (1) IT IS LEXICAL. Nine marker phrases, chosen as words any project would write rather than this one's idioms — "that is his call to make" was in the incident and is deliberately NOT a marker, on `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself`. It cannot tell an assertion from a quotation of one, and the test file records the moment that limit bit the test's own first draft. (2) IT NEVER SAYS THE PROSE IS WRONG, per `dec:report-dont-judge` — it names what matched, quotes the text, and asks. A node that quotes an old question is correct and looks identical from the outside; only a person can tell.","name":"A Decision that settles names the prose it governs that still says the question is open","provenance":"authored","status":"realized"}
